note.text:
Scientists have made discoveries that changed our lives.
• Isaac Newton described the laws of motion and gravity (1687).
• Michael Faraday showed how to make electricity with magnets (1831): this led to generators.
• Alexander Graham Bell made the telephone (1876).
• Marie Curie studied radioactivity (1898), used today in medicine.
• The Wright brothers made the first powered aeroplane flight (1903).
• Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin (1928), the first antibiotic.
• Arthur Zang, a Cameroonian engineer, created the Cardiopad (about 2011), a tablet that records heart tests and sends them to a doctor.
Science is done by people everywhere, including in Cameroon. You can be one of them.

worked_example.problem: A nurse in a village health centre records a patient's heart test on a tablet and sends it to a heart doctor in Yaoundé. Which discovery made this possible, and who made it?
steps: The tablet that records heart tests and sends them is the Cardiopad.
It was created by Arthur Zang, a Cameroonian engineer.
worked_example.answer: The Cardiopad, created by Arthur Zang.

cards.idea: Many great discoveries changed daily life: the telephone, electricity from generators, aeroplanes and medicines.
example: Bell → the telephone. Faraday → electricity from magnets. Fleming → penicillin.

cards.idea: Each discovery helps people in a different way: to talk, to travel, to have light and power, to stay healthy.
example: Penicillin cures infections. The telephone carries our voice far away.

check.prompt: Which discovery lets people talk to each other across long distances?

wrong.explain: The aeroplane lets people travel by air.
The laws of motion help engineers design machines and vehicles.
